title: MaterialsFile
description: The JSON shape of one file in `data/materials/`.

$schema.description:
Optional: the JSON Schema this file follows, so editors can check
it as you type (`"$schema": "../schema/materials.schema.json"`).

Colour.description:
The colours a material can be drawn in. A short fixed list rather than
any colour at all, so every terminal can show them (decision D16).

oneOf.description: Doors, so they stand out from the walls around them.

colour.description: The colour walls made of it are drawn in.

description.description: A sentence or two for look mode.

hardness.description: Vickers hardness (HV): how hard it is to scratch, drill or grind.

id.description: How data files refer to it, like `"steel"`.

melting_point.description:
Melting point in °C, or `None` for something that doesn't melt
(cotton chars and burns instead).

name.description: How it's shown to the player, like "Steel".

specific_heat.description: Specific heat in J/(kg·K): how much heat it takes to warm.

tags.description:
What kind of stuff it is, like `["metal"]`: a recipe can ask for
items of a material with a tag (only metal scrap patches the hull).
Optional: none.

thermal_conductivity.description:
Thermal conductivity in mW/(m·K) (thousandths, so insulators like
cotton at 0.04 W/(m·K) aren't rounded to nothing): how well heat
passes through.

worked_by.description:
The tool qualities that cut it, and the level each needs. Any one
is enough. Empty means nothing can cut it.
